_meta.description: GitLab Epic documentation templates — optimized for progressive disclosure, visual scannability, and decision-forward structure. Inspired by Google Design Docs, Amazon 6-Pagers, and Stripe engineering practices.

changelog.2.1.0: Removed TL;DR (merged into Objective), removed manual TOC (GitLab handles natively), renamed 'Metadata Header' to 'Epic Status'
changelog.2.1.1: Additive-only improvements: added titleFormat to User Stories, added hints/examples to underspecified sections, added mermaidDefaults/wordLimitConventions/collapsibleDefault/traceability to globalDefaults, standardized RACI and Risk hints, added categoryEnum to NFRs, added riskLevel field, added conditional to applicable sections
changelog.2.1.2: Added refinementMode, qualityRules, wordTargetInterpretation, and antiPatterns to globalDefaults. Added qualityGate to each template. Refinement now prioritizes density over length — tighten, don't expand.

wordLimitConventions.zeroMeaning: When target and max are both 0, the section is table-only or diagram-only — no prose word limit applies
wordLimitConventions.nullMeaning: Section intentionally has no word count constraint

mermaidDefaults.namingConvention: PascalCase short names, full names in node labels
mermaidDefaults.hint: Optimize for readability at 1200px width. Group related nodes with subgraphs. Keep labels concise (3-5 words max per node).

raciRules.hint: Each row must have exactly ONE Accountable person. Bold the R and A cells. If someone is both R and A, mark as R/A in bold.
raciRules.validation: Exactly one A per row is mandatory

riskLevels.full: Heat map (5×5 with colored emoji) + detailed register table + contingency column
riskLevels.standard: Register table with columns: Risk, Likelihood, Impact, Mitigation, Owner
riskLevels.light: Simple risk table without heat map or scoring

traceability.description: Cross-reference map showing how IDs trace across template types in a project pipeline

wordTargetInterpretation.target: IDEAL word count — the sweet spot. NOT a minimum to pad towards. Content that says everything needed in fewer words is BETTER, not worse.
wordTargetInterpretation.max: Hard ceiling. Never exceed. But hitting max usually means the section is bloated.
wordTargetInterpretation.sweetSpot: 60-85% of target is often the quality zone. Hitting exactly target usually means filler was added.
wordTargetInterpretation.rule: If the existing content already covers all required points below the target, DO NOT add words to reach the target. Shorter + complete > longer + padded.

refinementMode.description: Rules that apply when refining/editing an existing epic, NOT generating from scratch.
refinementMode.corePrinciple: Refinement means TIGHTEN, not EXPAND. The goal is to increase information density — more signal per sentence, fewer total sentences.

cut.description: Remove filler, redundancy, weasel words, and content that restates what's already said elsewhere. This is the #1 refinement action.
targets: Sentences that restate the Objective inside other sections
Transitional phrases that add no information ('It is important to note that...', 'As mentioned above...')
Hedging language ('It should be noted that...', 'We believe that...', 'It is worth considering...')
Generic statements that apply to any project ('Testing is important', 'Security must be considered')
Bullet points that say the same thing in different words

sharpen.description: Replace vague statements with specific, quantified, actionable ones.

examples.before: Ensure proper security measures are in place
examples.after: TLS 1.3 for transit, AES-256 at rest, IAM roles scoped to least-privilege

examples.before: The system should handle increased load
examples.after: Auto-scale from 3 to 12 pods at 70% CPU, supporting 10K→50K RPM

examples.before: Users should have a good experience
examples.after: Checkout completion in <90s, zero full-page reloads, WCAG 2.1 AA compliant

restructure.description: Move misplaced content to the correct section. Do NOT duplicate — move.
restructure.rule: If technical details appear in Business Context, move them to Proposed Design. If business justification appears in Implementation Plan, move it to Business Context. Each section should contain ONLY what its hint describes.

protected: Specific numbers, dates, dollar amounts, and quantified metrics
Links to external resources (Figma, Jira, docs)

lengthRules.existingShorterThanTarget: If existing content is shorter than target but covers all required points completely, DO NOT pad it. Mark as complete.
lengthRules.existingLongerThanMax: If existing content exceeds max, CUT to bring within max. Prioritize cutting filler over cutting substance.
lengthRules.existingAtTarget: If existing content is near target, focus on SHARPENING (replace vague with specific) not expanding.
lengthRules.defaultBehavior: Refinement should produce output that is the SAME length or SHORTER than input. If output is longer than input, justify every added sentence.

refinementMode.outputLengthCheck: After refinement, compare output word count to input word count. If output is >10% longer than input, re-examine and cut. Refinement that makes things longer has failed.

qualityRules.description: Quality criteria that apply to ALL sections in ALL templates, for both generation and refinement.
sentenceLevelRules: Every sentence must pass the 'so what?' test — if you remove it and nothing is lost, it shouldn't exist
No sentence should begin with 'It is important to...', 'It should be noted that...', 'We need to ensure that...', or similar throat-clearing
Prefer active voice: 'The service processes 10K requests/min' not 'Requests are processed by the service at a rate of 10K/min'
Lead with the specific, follow with the context — not the other way around
One idea per sentence. If a sentence has 'and' connecting two unrelated points, split it or cut one
sectionLevelRules: No section should repeat information from another section. If two sections say the same thing, one is wrong.
Every section must add NEW information not available in any other section
Tables should not have prose preambles that restate what the table shows — let the table speak
If a section only contains generic advice that applies to any project, it's empty. Fill it with project-specific content or remove it.
documentLevelRules: The Objective section should be sufficient for a reader to decide if they need to read more. If it isn't, fix it first.
A reader at the '2_minute_read' progressive disclosure level should understand the full scope, key decisions, and risks. If they can't, the document structure is wrong.
Consistency: same terminology throughout. If it's called 'order-service' in one place, don't call it 'OrderService' or 'the ordering module' elsewhere.

antiPatterns.description: Common LLM output patterns that indicate low quality. These should be actively detected and eliminated.

patterns.name: Echo Padding
patterns.description: Restating the Objective or Problem Statement inside other sections using slightly different words
patterns.detection: If any section's opening sentence could be swapped with the Objective and no one would notice, it's echo padding
patterns.fix: Delete the restated content. Start the section with its own unique first point.

patterns.name: Filler Bullets
patterns.description: Bullet points that state obvious truths: 'Ensure high availability', 'Follow security best practices', 'Maintain code quality'
patterns.detection: If a bullet applies to literally every software project ever built, it's filler
patterns.fix: Replace with project-specific measurable statement or delete entirely

patterns.name: Hedge Stacking
patterns.description: Multiple hedging qualifiers: 'We should potentially consider possibly exploring the option of...'
patterns.detection: More than one hedge word per sentence
patterns.fix: Make a direct statement or flag it as an Open Question

patterns.name: Premature Elaboration
patterns.description: Explaining concepts the audience already knows: 'Kubernetes, which is a container orchestration platform...'
patterns.detection: Inline definitions of terms the target audience uses daily
patterns.fix: If the term needs explanation, put it in the Glossary. Otherwise, just use the term.

patterns.name: Table Narration
patterns.description: Prose paragraphs that describe what a table already shows: 'As shown in the table below, Risk-001 has a likelihood of...'
patterns.detection: Prose that could be deleted and the table still conveys full meaning
patterns.fix: Delete the narration. Add a one-line summary only if it highlights a non-obvious insight.

patterns.name: Section Filler
patterns.description: Generic opening/closing sentences in every section: 'This section describes...', 'In summary, this section covered...'
patterns.detection: First or last sentence of a section that could apply to any document
patterns.fix: Delete entirely. Start with the first substantive point. End with the last substantive point.

patterns.name: Symmetric Padding
patterns.description: Making all bullet lists the same length by adding weak items to short lists
patterns.detection: A list where the last 1-2 items are noticeably more vague or generic than the first items
patterns.fix: 3 strong bullets > 6 bullets where half are filler. Cut the weak ones.

Epic Status.hint: Use reviewer status emoji (✅ ⏳ 🔄) for instant review-state visibility

Objective.hint: What are we doing, why, and what's the expected business outcome? This is the first thing anyone reads — make it count.
Objective.example: Implement an automated vendor onboarding portal to reduce average vendor setup time from 14 days to 2 days, eliminating $320K/year in manual processing costs and unblocking the procurement team's Q3 scale targets.

Business Context & Problem Statement.hint: Lead with data. What pain exists today? Quantify the cost of inaction.

Business Objectives.hint: SMART format — Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound

Scope & Non-Scope.hint: Non-scope is equally important as scope. List what this initiative deliberately excludes and why.

Stakeholders & RACI.hint: Each row must have exactly ONE Accountable person. Bold the R and A cells. If someone is both R and A, mark as R/A in bold.

Requirements.hint: Each requirement gets 30–80 words max. Use priority emoji for visual scanning. IDs should follow format BR-{nnn} for traceability.

Success Metrics.hint: Every metric must be quantified. 'Improve performance' is not a metric.

Risk Assessment.hint: Show 5×5 heat map first using colored emoji (🟢🟡🟠🔴), then detailed register table below. Risk IDs should follow format RISK-{nnn}. Score = Likelihood (1-5) × Impact (1-5).

Next Steps & Decision Log.hint: Use GitLab task lists (- [ ]) for action items. Decision log captures key choices made.

Glossary.hint: Use GitLab description list syntax for clean term definitions

business_requirement.description: Business requirements focusing on ROI, stakeholder value, strategic alignment, and measurable outcomes. Uses RACI matrices, risk heat maps, and SMART objectives.

qualityGate.description: Pre-output checklist. Every item must pass before finalizing. Applies to both generation and refinement.
checks: Objective is self-contained: a reader can decide whether to read further based on Objective alone
Every Business Objective is SMART — if any objective lacks a number or date, it fails
No requirement in the Requirements table is longer than 80 words
Every row in Success Metrics has a specific number in Baseline and Target columns — no 'TBD' or 'N/A'
Risk Assessment has at least 3 risks — if fewer, the analysis is superficial
No section restates the Objective in different words
RACI table has exactly one A (Accountable) per row
refinementSpecific: Output is same length or shorter than input — if longer, justify every added sentence
No new filler phrases were introduced (check antiPatterns list)
All specific numbers, dates, and names from the original are preserved
Vague statements were replaced with specific ones, not just reworded

Epic Status.hint: Use Stripe-style gavel block — each reviewer gets status emoji showing approval state

Objective.hint: What are we building, why, and what's the key architectural decision? One paragraph that gives full context.
Objective.example: Design an event-driven notification service to replace the current synchronous email pipeline, enabling sub-second delivery across email, SMS, and push channels while supporting 10x current throughput (50K→500K messages/hour) with independent channel scaling.

Context & Motivation.hint: What problem does this solve? What triggered this work? Include links to relevant issues/epics.

Goals & Non-Goals.hint: NON-GOALS are the most important part. List things that could reasonably be goals but are deliberately excluded.

Architecture Overview.hint: Include a mermaid architecture diagram. The diagram IS the source of truth — no stale images. Keep to 15 nodes max for readability.

Data Model & Storage.hint: Schema definitions, storage choices, data lifecycle

API Contracts.hint: Request/response examples in JSON code blocks. Use inline diff ({+ new +} / {- old -}) for changes.

Key Algorithms & Logic.conditional: Include only if non-trivial logic exists. Skip for straightforward CRUD operations.
Key Algorithms & Logic.hint: Only for non-trivial logic. Skip if straightforward CRUD.

Alternatives Considered.hint: ⭐ THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SECTION (per Google). Shows rigorous thinking. Each alternative gets 100–200 words. Include at least 2 genuine alternatives — not straw men.

Implementation Plan.hint: Break into shippable increments. Each phase should deliver testable value.

Risks & Mitigations.hint: Use standard likelihood values: Rare, Unlikely, Possible, Likely, Almost Certain. Use standard impact values: Negligible, Minor, Moderate, Major, Severe.

Open Questions.hint: Use GitLab task lists: - [ ] Question (@owner, due: date). Close as decisions are made.

Decision Log (ADRs).hint: MADR format: Status → Context → Decision Drivers → Considered Options → Decision Outcome

Definition of Done.hint: Use GitLab three-state task lists: [x] done, [ ] pending, [~] not applicable

Appendix.hint: Extended analysis, raw data, detailed calculations. Use <details> tags.

technical_design.description: Technical design documents following Google's design doc philosophy — context, goals/non-goals, proposed design, alternatives considered, and cross-cutting concerns. Emphasizes demonstrating rigorous thinking through explicit trade-off analysis.

qualityGate.description: Pre-output checklist. Every item must pass before finalizing.
checks: Objective states the key architectural decision, not just the feature being built
Non-Goals list has at least 2 items that could reasonably be goals — not straw men
Alternatives Considered has at least 2 genuine alternatives with real pros, not just the chosen option
Architecture diagram exists and matches the prose — no components mentioned in text but missing from diagram
Every API contract has a working JSON request/response example
No section opens with 'This section describes...' or 'In this section we will...'
Cross-Cutting Concerns contain project-specific details, not generic advice
refinementSpecific: Output is same length or shorter than input
Technical details were not moved into Business Context or Objective
Trade-off analysis in Alternatives Considered was preserved or strengthened, not diluted
No new throat-clearing phrases ('It is important to note...') were introduced

Objective.hint: What user problem are we solving, and how will we know we've solved it? Lead with the user impact.
Objective.example: Enable users to save and reuse delivery addresses, reducing checkout abandonment by 15% and average checkout time from 4.2 minutes to under 90 seconds for returning customers.

Problem Statement.hint: Lead with evidence — user research data, support ticket volume, funnel drop-off rates. Not assumptions.

User Stories.template:
**US-{nn}: {title}**
As a [persona], I want [action] so that [outcome]
**Acceptance Criteria:** [testable criterion]
User Stories.hint: Each user story MUST begin with a bold, scannable title in the format 'US-01: One-Click Reorder' followed by the As a… statement. Titles should be unique, concise (3-6 words), and action-oriented. Each story must map to at least one testable acceptance criterion listed directly below it.
User Stories.example:
**US-01: Save Delivery Address**
As a returning customer, I want to save my delivery address so that I don't have to re-enter it on every order.
**Acceptance Criteria:** User can save up to 5 addresses; saved addresses appear as selectable options at checkout; user can edit or delete saved addresses from account settings.

Scope & Non-Scope.hint: Non-scope prevents scope creep. Be explicit about what's out for V1 and what's deferred to V2.

Functional Requirements.hint: Each requirement must be atomic (one testable behavior per row), reference a User Story by ID (e.g. US-01), and include pass/fail acceptance criteria. Priority must use emoji indicators. IDs should follow format FR-{nnn} for traceability.

User Flows.hint: Include mermaid flowcharts for happy path AND key error paths. Don't just document the sunshine scenario. Keep to 15 nodes max per diagram for readability.

Non-Functional Requirements.hint: Use standard categories from categoryEnum. Be specific and quantified: 'P99 latency < 200ms' not 'should be fast'. Every requirement must have a measurable target and a method to verify it.

Launch Plan.hint: Feature flag strategy, rollout percentage plan, rollback criteria, A/B test design if applicable

UX/Design.hint: Link to Figma/mockups. Describe key interaction patterns and accessibility requirements.

Dependencies & Risks.hint: Use standard likelihood values: Rare, Unlikely, Possible, Likely, Almost Certain. Use standard impact values: Negligible, Minor, Moderate, Major, Severe.

Competitive Analysis.hint: How do competitors solve this problem? What can we learn?

feature_specification.description: Feature specifications that bridge product and engineering — evidence-based problem statements, user stories with acceptance criteria, explicit edge cases, launch plans with rollback criteria, and measurable success metrics.

qualityGate.description: Pre-output checklist. Every item must pass before finalizing.
checks: Problem Statement leads with evidence (data, ticket counts, metrics) — not opinions or assumptions
Every User Story has a bold title in US-{nn} format before the As a… statement
Every User Story maps to at least one Functional Requirement via ID reference
Edge Cases table has at least 5 scenarios — if fewer, the happy-path bias is too strong
Non-Functional Requirements use specific numbers ('P99 < 200ms') not adjectives ('fast', 'responsive')
Launch Plan includes explicit rollback criteria — not just rollout steps
No section contains generic filler like 'ensure a good user experience'
refinementSpecific: Output is same length or shorter than input
User Story titles were not removed or made generic during refinement
Acceptance Criteria from original were preserved — not dropped or made vaguer
No new bullet points were added that fail the 'applies to every project' test

Objective.hint: What does this API do, who consumes it, and what's the key design principle?
Objective.example: Provide a RESTful API for the Partner Portal to manage merchant onboarding workflows, consumed by the Partner Dashboard (React) and three external integration partners. Key principle: idempotent operations with optimistic concurrency control.

Overview & Authentication.hint: Base URLs per environment, auth mechanism (OAuth2/API key/JWT), token lifecycle, scopes/permissions

Resource Definitions.hint: One table per resource. Include validation rules and constraints. Mark required fields clearly.

Endpoints.hint: Working examples are mandatory. Use diff code blocks ({+ new +} / {- old -}) for versioned changes.

Error Handling.hint: Standardized error envelope. Include request_id for debugging. Group by category (auth, validation, server).

Pagination & Rate Limiting.hint: Exact numbers: requests/minute, burst limit, pagination cursor vs offset, max page size, rate limit headers

Webhooks & Events.hint: Include payload examples. Specify at-least-once vs at-most-once delivery. Document idempotency keys.
Webhooks & Events.conditional: Include only if API has event-driven components

Versioning & Deprecation.hint: URL vs header versioning, backward compatibility guarantees, deprecation timeline, sunset headers

Changelog.hint: Use inline diff syntax for schema changes. Flag breaking changes with > [!caution] alerts.

Testing & Sandbox.hint: Sandbox URLs, test credentials, mock data, Postman collection link

api_specification.description: API specifications modeled after Stripe's gold standard — working examples for every endpoint, standardized error envelopes, explicit rate limits, webhook delivery guarantees, and versioning strategy. Developer experience is the primary design constraint.

qualityGate.description: Pre-output checklist. Every item must pass before finalizing.
checks: Every endpoint has a working cURL example that a developer could copy-paste and run
Every endpoint has at least one error response documented — not just the happy path
Error codes follow a consistent naming convention (e.g., SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE) across all endpoints
Rate limits are exact numbers, not 'reasonable limits' or 'subject to change'
Resource schema tables have Example column filled for every field — no empty cells
Authentication section specifies token lifetime and refresh mechanism
refinementSpecific: Output is same length or shorter than input
No working code examples were removed or broken during refinement
Endpoint paths and HTTP methods were not changed unless explicitly requested
Schema field names and types were preserved exactly

Objective.hint: What infrastructure are we building/changing, why, and what are the key SLA targets?
Objective.example: Deploy a multi-region active-active PostgreSQL cluster on AWS to achieve 99.99% availability (currently 99.9%), reduce cross-region read latency from 180ms to <40ms, and support the projected 3x traffic growth through Q4 2025.

Business Context.hint: Why does the business need this infrastructure? What happens if we don't build it?

SLA/SLO Requirements.hint: Availability, latency percentiles, throughput, error rate. Current vs target. Every SLO must have an error budget calculated.

Architecture Overview.hint: Mermaid architecture diagram is mandatory. Show all services, data stores, network boundaries, and traffic flow. Keep to 15 nodes max for readability — use subgraphs to group related components.

Component Design.hint: One subsection per major component: compute, storage, networking, CDN, queues, etc. Each component must answer: how does it fail, how do we know, how do we recover?

Environments & CI/CD.hint: Include pipeline diagram (mermaid) showing build → test → stage → prod flow

Disaster Recovery.hint: Include explicit RPO/RTO targets per failure scenario. When was the last DR drill?

Scaling Strategy.hint: Horizontal vs vertical. Auto-scaling policies. Include cost implications at scale.

Cost Analysis.hint: Include current spend vs projected spend. Flag top 3 cost drivers.

Operational Runbooks.hint: Index of runbooks with links. Detailed procedures live in separate docs.

Migration/Cutover Plan.hint: If this replaces existing infra, include cutover steps and rollback procedure

infrastructure_design.description: Infrastructure design documents emphasizing operational readiness — explicit SLA/SLO targets, cost analysis, disaster recovery with tested RPO/RTO, observability with alerting rules, and scaling strategies with cost implications. Every component must answer: how does it fail, how do we know, how do we recover?

qualityGate.description: Pre-output checklist. Every item must pass before finalizing.
checks: SLA/SLO table has Current Value filled for every metric — shows we measured before designing
Every component in Component Design answers: how does it fail, how do we know, how do we recover
Disaster Recovery table has 'Last Tested' column filled — untested DR plans are fiction
Cost Analysis flags the top 3 cost drivers explicitly
Scaling Strategy includes cost-at-max for every component — scaling without cost awareness is dangerous
Architecture diagram matches the Component Design sections — no orphan components in either
refinementSpecific: Output is same length or shorter than input
Specific cost figures, SLO numbers, and capacity numbers were preserved exactly
No alerting rules or runbook links were removed
Generic statements like 'follow security best practices' were replaced with specifics, not just kept

Objective.hint: What are we migrating, from where to where, when, and what's the rollback window?
Objective.example: Migrate 2.3TB of customer order data from on-prem Oracle 12c to AWS Aurora PostgreSQL 15 with zero-downtime cutover on March 15, 2025. Rollback window: 72 hours post-cutover. Dual-write period: 2 weeks.

Current State.hint: Architecture diagram of current system. Include known pain points, technical debt, and failure modes.

Target State.hint: Architecture diagram of target system. Highlight what changes and what stays the same.

Migration Strategy.hint: Big-bang vs phased vs trickle. Lift-and-shift vs re-platform vs re-architect. Justify the choice.

Scope & Non-Scope.hint: What's included in this migration phase? What's explicitly deferred?

RACI Matrix.hint: Each row must have exactly ONE Accountable person. Bold the R and A cells. Migration plans cross multiple teams — RACI eliminates 'I thought they were doing that' failures.

Risk Assessment.hint: ⭐ HIGHEST-STAKES DOCUMENT TYPE. Risk assessment must be thorough. Include contingency plans (what we do if the mitigation fails), not just mitigations. Risk IDs should follow format RISK-{nnn}. Score = Likelihood (1-5) × Impact (1-5).

Timeline & Milestones.hint: Include Gantt chart via mermaid. Each milestone needs explicit go/no-go criteria.

Cutover Plan.hint: Step-by-step numbered procedure. Include time estimates per step, responsible person, and verification checks.

Rollback Plan.hint: Explicit triggers (what conditions activate rollback). Step-by-step procedure. Maximum rollback window. Data reconciliation steps.

Dry Run Plan.hint: When, how many dry runs, success criteria

Data Security & Compliance.hint: Data classification, encryption in transit/at rest, access controls during migration, audit trail, compliance requirements

Communication Plan.hint: Who needs to know what, when? Include customer-facing comms if applicable.

Post-Migration Support Plan.hint: Hypercare period, escalation paths, known issues watchlist, performance monitoring period

Lessons Learned.hint: Fill in post-migration. Template exists so it doesn't get forgotten.

migration_plan.description: Migration plans as operational playbooks — current/target state architectures, explicit RACI ownership, risk heat maps with contingency plans, step-by-step cutover and rollback procedures, dry run plans, and communication matrices. Designed for the highest-stakes document type in engineering.

qualityGate.description: Pre-output checklist. Every item must pass before finalizing.
checks: Current State and Target State both have architecture diagrams — text-only descriptions fail during execution
Risk Assessment has at least 5 risks with Contingency plans (not just Mitigations) — this is the highest-stakes doc type
Cutover Plan has time estimates for every step and a named responsible person
Rollback Plan has explicit trigger conditions (what metrics/events activate rollback)
Dry Run Plan specifies how many dry runs and success criteria for each
RACI Matrix has exactly one A per row and covers at least: cutover, rollback, communication, validation
Every milestone in Timeline has Go/No-Go criteria — milestones without criteria are just dates
refinementSpecific: Output is same length or shorter than input
No steps were removed from Cutover or Rollback procedures — steps can be reworded but not dropped
Time estimates, dates, and rollback windows were preserved exactly
Risk contingency plans were not downgraded to generic mitigations

full_read: all sections including Cutover and Rollback procedures

Objective.hint: What systems are being integrated, what data flows between them, and what's the SLA?
Objective.example: Integrate Salesforce CRM with the internal Order Management System (OMS) via event-driven messaging to synchronize customer and order data in near-real-time (<5s propagation), replacing the current nightly batch sync that causes 12-hour data staleness.

Integration Overview.hint: System context diagram showing all participating systems, direction of data flow, and integration pattern (sync/async/event). Keep to 8 participants max for readability.

Systems & Endpoints.hint: One row per system. Include all environments (dev/staging/prod) if URLs differ.

Data Contract & Mappings.hint: Include schema validation rules. Use inline diff for contract changes. Document null-handling and default values for every field.

Error / Retry Path.hint: DO NOT SKIP. Error flows are where integrations actually fail.

Recovery / Reconciliation Path.conditional: Include if data consistency guarantees require reconciliation between systems.

Error Handling & Recovery.hint: Retry policies: max attempts, backoff strategy (exponential/linear), circuit breaker thresholds. Every error scenario must have a defined detection method and resolution path.

Monitoring & Alerting.hint: Monitor integration health, not just system health. Track: message throughput, error rate, latency, queue depth.

Performance & SLAs.hint: Define SLAs for end-to-end data propagation time, not just individual system response time.

Versioning & Backward Compatibility.hint: How are breaking changes handled across system boundaries? Contract versioning strategy.

Fallback & Degradation.hint: What happens when the integration is down? Graceful degradation strategy, cached responses, circuit breakers.

Operational Runbook.hint: Troubleshooting guide: common failures, diagnostic steps, resolution procedures. Wrap in <details> tags.

integration_spec.description: Integration specifications as enforceable contracts — explicit data mappings, sequence diagrams for happy AND error paths, retry policies with circuit breaker thresholds, SLA definitions with breach escalation, and monitoring that tracks integration health specifically. Error flows are required, not optional.

qualityGate.description: Pre-output checklist. Every item must pass before finalizing.
checks: Both Happy Path AND Error/Retry Path have sequence diagrams — error path is NOT optional
Error Handling table has retry policy details (max attempts, backoff type, circuit breaker threshold) for every scenario
Data Contract table has Transformation column filled — empty means 'nobody thought about this'
Monitoring table tracks integration-level metrics (message throughput, queue depth) not just system metrics (CPU, memory)
SLA table has Breach Escalation column filled — SLAs without escalation paths are aspirational, not enforceable
Every system in Systems & Endpoints has Auth Mechanism and Rate Limits filled
refinementSpecific: Output is same length or shorter than input
Data field mappings were preserved exactly — field names and types cannot be changed during refinement
Retry policies and circuit breaker thresholds were not removed or made vague
Sequence diagrams were not simplified to the point of losing error handling steps

full_read: all sections including sequence diagrams and error handling
